description.narrative: The Government of Sudan (GoS) is responding to urgent needs to stabilize the economy and begin a long process of clearing arrears to MFIs as part of the Sudan's larger macroeconomic stabilization and integration. These measures are expected to include exchange rate liberalization/unification and reallocation of public resources away from commodity subsidies, tax exemptions, towards social and development needs. These fiscal adjustments are expected to contribute to furthering an already deteriorating economic situation in Sudan which has impacted vulnerable people's abilities to cover basic needs. These challenges facing households are compounded by the economic shutdown recently imposed to mitigate the effects of the Corona Virus pandemic (COVID 19) in some regions of Sudan. Accordingly, the GoS has requested support from the donor community to establish the Sudan Family Support Program (SFSP) to provide cash transfers to 80 percent of the population, i.e., to about 32.5 million individuals, with an annual cost of US $1.9 billion. The SFSP would continue for up to two years, depending on financing availability. The GoS will contribute its own budget to the SFSP, particularly as the program enters later phases and transitions to the longer-term support to permanent social safety nets. The project's development objective is to deliver cash transfer support to Sudanese households affected by expected economic reforms and other short-term shocks. To this end, the project includes three components. These are: Component 1, Provision of Cash Transfers, to provide cash transfers to selected households; Component 2, Establish Delivery Systems and Build Institutional Capacity; and Component 3, Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Learning.The project will support the first phase of the government program, providing cash transfers during the startup period of the program. The project would provide cash transfers of $5 per person per month to 5.5 million people in 1.1 million families for a total cost of US$350 million for the transfers. This phase will prepare for later expansion to a full program, depending on lessons learned and resources available. The plan for the full-fledged program is to provide cash transfers of $5 per person per month to approximately 80 percent of the population, i.e. 32.5 million people for an annual cost of $1,950 million. The first phase will build on lessons from the pilot initiated in July 2020, and will support the development of building blocks necessary for establishment of a more effective social Safety Net system in Sudan. Specific focus during this phase will be on transforming the existing institutional and administrative structures to consolidate permanent institutional arrangements in order to design, implement and monitor the social safety net as well as support informed decision making in the context of the national social protection framework. The first states and subsequent scale up will consider issues of; (i) poverty head count; (ii) existing implementation capacity of safety nets programs; (ii) payment infrastructure and (iv) presence or absence of UN agencies in those states and (v) rural/urban consideration or a combination of all these factors. Based on these factors, it is recommended that phase 1 project implementation will start in the states of (i)Khartoum, (ii) Red Sea; (iii) South Darfur and (iv) Kassala. Based on the external resource flows the design of the second phase will start immediately after the delivery of the first phase.

The objective is to deliver cash transfers and improve safety net systems to support the Sudanese families in the Recipient's territory affected by expected economic reforms and other short-term shocks.

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries enrolled in mobile money

comment.narrative: The target was met. Of all the payments mechanisms, the project encouraged the use of mobile money to foster financial inclusion.

title.narrative: Number of families receiving cash/income support

comment.narrative: The project paid cash transfers to approximately 1.5 million families, nearly 70 percent of the project ‘s target. This notable achievement was realized in eight months due to the project pause following the military takeover that triggered OP 7:30.

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries enrolled in basic bank accounts

comment.narrative: Some 1.6 million beneficiaries were enrolled in bank accounts (100 percent achievement) despite the low banking penetration in Sudan. This is a considerable achievement in a conflict country with limited infrastructure facilities and a cash-based economy, as only 15.3 percent of the population has a financial account.

title.narrative: Number of states covered by the SFSP program

comment.narrative: The objective of the Government's Sudan Family Support Program was to provide cash assistance to all eligible citizens of Sudan in all the 18 states. The parent project supported Phase 1 of the Government Program, covering 4 states: Khartoum, Red Sea, South Darfur, and Kassala. The AF planned to expand the coverage, adding 8 states (South Kordofan, Blue Nile, Sinnar, Central Darfur, North Kordofan, East Darfur, West Kordofan, and White Nile WFP covered an additional two states. Thus, the SFSP covered 12 states of the Government program, WFP covered 2 states.).

title.narrative: Average number of days for funds to reach beneficiary accounts

comment.narrative: The project achieved about 70 percent of the target. This is a substantial result given the challenging FCV environment, including the project pause after a short eight-month implementation period.

title.narrative: Percentage of complaints resolved in 15 days or less through GRM

comment.narrative: The resolving of cases significantly improved as it reached 1,017 of the total 1,182 cases received (86%), due to the coordination of the call center with a free hot line link, and regular update of the referral pathway and Q&A documents. Also, the call center scale up was on-track with proper scale up in terms of staffing, capacity, equipment and performance. Besides, the call center explored ways to process social media and email complaints for better GRM accessibility.

title.narrative: Time in days between generation of payroll and fund transfer to PSPs
National registry platform that functions across the country is strengthened

baseline.value: National platform is functioning, but has low coverage and needs efficiency improvements.

target.value: National registry platform is covering 80% of the population in the regions covered by the project.

comment.narrative: The project strengthened the national registry platform, following the signing of the MOU with the Ministry of Interior, and provision of equipment and mobile registration units.

actual.value: The national registry platform was upgraded, following the signing of the MOU with the Mistry of Interior. National ID covered 80% of the population in the four regions (Khartoum, Red Sea, South Darfur and Kassala) targeted by the project. Work plan and budget developed to provide the platform with necessary equipment and mobile registration units.

title.narrative: A hybrid system for tracking enquiries, complaints, and grievances (GRM) has been established

comment.narrative: The project's GRM system was established. All operators were dedicated to handle incoming calls, which impacted the number of received complaints as it spiked from 978 cases in July to reach 1,182 cases in October 2021.

Outreach campaign implemented in 8 states (Kassala, White Nile, South Darfur, West Darfur, North Kurdofan, East Darfur, Red Sea, and Khartoum). Messages on registration and payment disseminated via 4 national radios and TVs channels to reach all who access radio and TV broadcast in Sudan.

title.narrative: SFSP MIS system has been developed and deployed

comment.narrative: SFSP MIS had Registration/Enrollment, Payment, Case Management, M&E, and Reporting/Data Analytics modules along with technical documentation and user manuals. These modules were developed, tested and implemented. The MIS system had also data sharing platform and linkages with National Civil Registry administrative data sources. The MIS had linkages setup with payment providers for digital payments, facilitating SFSP payments.

title.narrative: SFSP branded as a national, well-defined and quasi universal program

comment.narrative: A brand for the program was developed (brand name Thamarat). A brand is the name, term, design, logo, tagline, content, and other features that will be used in mainstreaming SFSP as a national, well-defined, and quasi universal program. Brand worked as a program identity and supported marketing SFSP objectives which aim to mitigate the effects of the economic hardship and improve Sudanese living conditions. Branding includes series of processes for planning, producing, testing, and publicizing the communication and community outreach material.
